raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add `adaptive_verification_floor` to speculative decoding: verify every scheduled
draft when the number of requests with scheduled drafts is at or below the floor.
This gives deployments a fixed-verification regime at low concurrency when
adaptive budgeting varies with the cost profile or acceptance estimates.

## Claims

- Nonnegative integer, default `0` (disabled). For example, add
  `"enable_adaptive_verification": true, "adaptive_verification_floor": 8`
  to an existing speculative config to retain all scheduled drafts at up to
  eight requests with scheduled drafts.
- Requests without scheduled drafts, including draftless decodes, do not count.
  Above the threshold,
  normal adaptive selection applies. The existing logits-memory cap still applies.
- No new device synchronization, kernels, or changes to the default behavior.

## Validation

Picked https://github.com/benchislett/vllm/pull/19 at `5dfbf76226` (original
commit `22223b70a5`). The contributor reports **31 passing tests**, including the
adaptive-verification suite and floor serving test, plus clean pre-commit.
These results were not independently rerun for the cherry-pick. The updated
unit case covers excluding draftless decodes from the count.

Rebased at `2785484ee2` onto upstream `41f5146b5b`:

- Focused local config/adaptive tests: **25 passed**.
- Local runner/batch-ordering tests: **33 passed**.
- Pre-commit passed on all changed files.

The rebase preserves upstream's optional host-copy argument and adapts the floor
test to the four-value draft-reallocation result. The floor's budget logic is
unchanged. Full GPU/model validation was not repeated after the rebase; the
previous results below apply to their recorded commits. No performance gains
are claimed.

Prior validation at `74310f4c8a` (LLM test at `52a2c63f72`):

- GB300 adaptive-verification suite: **23 passed in 27.92s**, including
  the six new floor cases (`pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -q`).
- Final LLM test at `52a2c63f72`: **1 passed in 107.31s**, serving batches
  1, 2, and 3 at floor 2 with positive draft acceptance in every batch:
  `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py::test_dspark_adaptive_verification_floor -v -s`.

| Chat GSM8K smoke | Correct | Invalid answers |
|---|---:|---:|
| Actual base `a0544b13f2` | 28/32 (87.5%) | 0/32 |
| Floor 2 at `74310f4c8a` | 28/32 (87.5%) | 0/32 |

Both servers passed chat and raw-completion probes. Both smoke runs generated
4,773 output tokens. This small sample does not establish accuracy equivalence.

Two environment issues delayed serving validation: test dependencies installed
cu130 TorchAudio beside cu132 PyTorch (removed the unused audio package), and
the long Lustre TMPDIR exceeded ZMQ's Unix-socket path limit (using project-local
`VLLM_RPC_BASE_PATH=.tmp`). The latter occurred on the actual base before engine
startup. Neither required a feature-code change.

GPU coverage exercises the default, inclusive boundary, mixed prefill/decode,
draftless decodes, memory cap, and the reallocated device offsets. The LLM test
serves batches of 1, 2, and 3 at floor 2 and requires positive draft acceptance.
Both suites are selected by existing Buildkite steps.

Actual-base and candidate chat GSM8K smoke settings: Qwen/Qwen3-4B-FP8 with
deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7, TP1, 7 draft tokens, thinking disabled,
greedy, 32 questions, 5-shot, concurrency 2, 1024 output tokens.
These are smoke checks, not reference-score reproductions or performance claims.

<details>
<summary>Smoke reproduction settings</summary>

Both runs use the same editable precompiled environment, checking out the actual
base or feature commit before starting a fresh server. Set
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`,
`VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=256`, and
`VLLM_RPC_BASE_PATH=.tmp` (create `.tmp` first).

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B-FP8 --served-model-name model --port 8000 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7","num_speculative_tokens":7,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
```

For the feature run, add `"adaptive_verification_floor":2` to the speculative
config. The eval wrapper calls the existing upstream evaluator as follows
(`temperature=0`, `seed=42` are its defaults):

```python
from tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval import evaluate_gsm8k
evaluate_gsm8k(model="model", use_chat_completions=True, port=8000,
              max_tokens=1024, num_questions=32, num_shots=5,
              max_concurrency=2)
```

Target revision: `96b30dc13593a244a5e59e84687309f53c375cfa`;
drafter revision: `3457dff1417cb84927f6098a5fcb7cee85c934b7`.

</details>

## Details

The manager counts requests with scheduled drafts and selects the maximum safe
draft budget at or below the floor, skipping confidence/cost estimates and
reusing the common budget bookkeeping. Existing compaction and reallocation handle that budget. The floor may
increase verification work for low-acceptance drafts; it does not increase the
number of drafts scheduled or override memory limits. With floor 2, two drafting
requests plus a draftless decode now retain all scheduled drafts, subject to
the memory cap; the earlier implementation applied adaptive scoring in this case.

Open upstream PR searches for adaptive verification and adaptive/floor found no
matching configurable decode-count floor. Related suffix-decoding PR
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60339 mentions low-concurrency trimming
but implements a different drafter. The author reviewed the fork PR before
requesting this upstream submission. Codex assisted with implementation,
documentation, and validation.

Developed and validated from upstream `a0544b13f2ee6424d3aa6d03a00e1c745218dee9`.
Supersedes the reviewed fork PR https://github.com/benchislett/vllm/pull/18.

@@ -50,6 +50,19 @@ vllm serve MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4-DFlash \
 
 Set `enable_adaptive_verification: false` to verify the full block for every request.
 
+To keep low-concurrency verification independent of confidence and cost-profile
+variance, set `adaptive_verification_floor` in the speculative config alongside
+`enable_adaptive_verification: true`. For example,
+`"adaptive_verification_floor": 8` verifies all scheduled draft tokens when **8 or
+fewer requests have scheduled drafts**. Above 8, the usual adaptive budget
+applies. Requests without scheduled drafts, such as prefills, do not count toward
+the floor. The default is `0`, which disables the floor, and negative values are
+rejected.
+
+The floor does not override the rejection sampler's logits-memory limit or
+increase the number of drafts scheduled. It can increase verification work when
+draft acceptance is low. It has no effect when adaptive verification is disabled.
+
 ## Requirements and limitations
 
 - The attention backend must tolerate device-decided query lengths, since the CPU lengths only bound them from above. Backends that plan off the CPU lengths are excluded by the attention selector, and rejected at startup for models that hard-wire their backend.

+def test_adaptive_verification_floor_validation(floor):

+    )

+            SpeculativeConfig(**kwargs)
+    else:
+        assert SpeculativeConfig(**kwargs).adaptive_verification_floor == floor
